subject: PraxisMed Q4 term extension & GPU commit — proposed capacity sprint
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Rao <sam@praxismed.com>, procurement@praxismed.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: PraxisMed Q4 term extension & GPU commit — proposed capacity sprint

Hi Sam / procurement team,

Thanks again for a productive call this week. Per our conversation, attached is a short proposal and the QPS growth model that underpins our capacity recommendation for your upcoming renewal. Summary up front:

- Current committed capacity: 12 reserved GPUs (mixed A100 / H100 class).
- Observed baseline: ~170 QPS average over the last 30d (peak 310 QPS).
- PraxisMed forecast (you provided): projected traffic rise to ~420 QPS steady-state within 9–12 months as new triage and billing features ship.

Our recommendation (detailed in the attached PDF and CSV): increase committed capacity to 22 GPUs (10 additional), with a 6-GPU reserved burst pool for short-lived peaks. This configuration targets a sustained 420 QPS across your primary model family with a 95th percentile serving latency SLA of <=120ms for 2k token contexts.

Key commercial points: 12-month term extension, step-down pricing after month 6 if utilization thresholds are not met, and a 30% credit for three production canary weeks (to validate traffic and model variants before ramping fully). Monthly committed cost estimate included in the PDF.

Next steps I'd propose:
1) Quick 30-min ops/infra sync (Monica + Karthik + your infra) to validate the burst profile and canary plan.
2) Procurement to confirm target term & PO cadence so we can prepare a DocuSign term sheet.

Attachment: praxis_dedicated_proposal_v3.pdf (proposal summary), qps-growth-model.csv (breakdown & assumptions).

If helpful, I can include a model-variant plan (smaller model fallback + quantized path) as part of the canary.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.ai]

---
Attachment stubs:
- praxis_dedicated_proposal_v3.pdf (6 pages, tables: GPU counts, monthly cost, SLAs)
- qps-growth-model.csv (monthly QPS, 95th pct, token-per-request assumptions)
From: Sam Rao <sam@sam@praxismed.com>

Date: 2027-04-25T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PraxisMed Q4 term extension & GPU commit — proposed capacity sprint

Jordan — thanks, reviewed quickly. A few clarifying Qs before we loop procurement: 

1) How deterministic is the 420 QPS target? Our product roadmap has a few toggles — are you assuming full adoption?
2) What's the failure/fallback plan if traffic spikes above reserve (e.g., Black Friday-like scenario)?
3) Can you confirm whether autoscale over the committed pool is included or billed separately?

Also, procurement wants an explicit canary plan and a short-term credit if we exercise the canary and decide to scale down after.

Sam
VP Product, PraxisMed
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Rao <sam@praxismed.com>, procurement@praxismed.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-25T13:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PraxisMed Q4 term extension & GPU commit — proposed capacity sprint

Sam — great questions. Looping in Monica (CS lead) and Karthik (infra/solutions) to give a tight technical and commercial answer. Quick answers inline: 

1) Determinism: the 420 QPS number is conservative-high from your shared roadmap (we used 60% adoption of new features over 9 months). The CSV shows a sensitivity band down to 330 QPS and up to 520 QPS. We recommend committing to the middle-case but building guardrails (see canary).

2) Failure / spike handling: reserved burst pool (6 GPUs) + cross-region fallback; beyond that we can route excess to a lower-cost model variant (quantized 4-bit) at slightly higher latency but reduced cost. For extreme spikes we have the option of temporary burst credits from Redwood Dedicated for up to 72 hours (subject to advance approval).

3) Autoscale: autoscale across unreserved spare capacity is included in the Dedicated plan (within committed pool). Additional elastic capacity beyond committed + burst pool is billed as overage at a higher hourly rate; we can cap that and surface alerts.

Monica / Karthik — two asks: can you review the proposed GPU count and the SLA numbers? Also, Monica, please draft a 3-week canary plan text we can send to procurement (dates, metrics to validate, rollback criteria, credit mechanics).

Thanks,
Jordan
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Sam Rao <sam@praxismed.com>

Date: 2027-04-25T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PraxisMed Q4 term extension & GPU commit — proposed capacity sprint

Adding technical details / capacity math so procurement and infra can see rationale. Numbers assume Llama-family 13–33B class mixed-inference (8–12 tokens per request average across structured prompts):

Assumptions pulled from qps-growth-model.csv:
- Target steady QPS: 420 requests/sec.
- Avg tokens per request (including response): 180 tokens.
- Avg generation throughput per GPU (H100-equivalent, quantized pipeline): ~2.0M tokens/min (~33k tokens/sec) for mixed-batch steady state.

Capacity calc (steady state):
- Needed tokens/sec = 420 req/sec * 180 tokens = 75,600 tokens/sec.
- GPU tokens/sec per H100-equivalent = 33,000 tokens/sec.
- Required GPUs (pure compute) = 75,600 / 33,000 ≈ 2.29 => 23 GPUs to allow for batch inefficiencies, KV cache misses, routing overhead, and 95th pctl target.

Recommended footprint: 23 GPUs committed total broken down as:
- 17 GPUs sized for steady-state serving (primary pool)
- 6 GPUs reserved for burst / canary / model-variant fallback (on the same reservation)

Why larger than the initial 22? I rounded to 23 to include a small headroom buffer. If PraxisMed wants a smaller commit with the same SLA we can structure a staged ramp: 18 GPUs committed + 5-month review with an option to add 5 more at predefined pricing.

GPU class recommendation: H100-equivalent for main pool (model family performance), with a small group of A100-class for cheaper quantized fallback lanes. Quantization to q4f16 gives ~1.6–1.8x token throughput improvement and is part of the canary validation.

Operational notes:
- We will provision traffic routing policy to prefer primary pool, then burst, then quantized fallback.
- Canary plan should measure p95 latency, error rate, and token cost per 1M tokens.
- Billing: committed monthly fee for 23 GPUs, with an overage cap and pre-approved burst credit (72h).

I can produce a short one-pager with the math and a staged ramp option if you want to present it to legal/procurement.

-Karthik
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: PraxisMed Q4 term extension & GPU commit — proposed capacity sprint

Sam — following internal review we've formalized two options for your procurement team: 

Option A (recommended, single-step commit):
- Commit: 23 GPUs (17 steady + 6 burst)
- Term: 12 months
- Canary: 3 production weeks during months 1–2, 30% credit on month 1 committed fees if rollback chosen within 60 days
- SLA: 95th pct latency <=120ms for 2k token contexts; monthly uptime target 99.9%
- Estimated monthly committed cost: $185,000 (line items in attached PDF)

Option B (staged ramp, lower initial risk):
- Commit: 18 GPUs initial (13 steady + 5 burst)
- Term: 12 months with predefined ramp clauses to add 5 GPUs at month 4 or month 7 at fixed pricing tiers
- Canary: same 3-week plan, credit mechanics adjusted pro-rata
- Estimated monthly committed cost (initial): $148,000

If procurement is comfortable with Option A we will prepare an updated term sheet and DocuSign. If you prefer Option B we can include the ramp triggers (utilization thresholds) in the PO. Monica will follow up with the canary plan doc and the specific success metrics to validate model quality and cost per 1M tokens.

Looking forward to the quick sync — how does Thursday 10:00am PT look for everyone?

Best,
Jordan
